issues.legal_issue: Retrospective validation of a subletting does not protect a later transfer by the subtenant when the original subtenant was not in possession at the commencement of the validating measure.
material_facts: The contractual tenant sublet the premises to an individual before the validating measure took effect.
The individual transferred the business and possession of the premises to a company, which was in possession when the measure took effect; the individual was not then in possession.
The company claimed protection as a subtenant after being dispossessed in execution of a decree against the contractual tenant.
The company's transfer was not within a class of transfers permitted by a government notification.
issues.conclusion: The company was not protected by the retrospective validation because it was a subsequent assignee from the subtenant, not the subtenant itself, and the original subtenant was not in possession when the validating measure took effect.
issues.legal_principle: Section 15(2) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947 validates a pre-existing sublease, assignment, or transfer made by a tenant only where the person in whose favour it was made entered into possession before the validating measure and continued in possession when it commenced; it does not validate a later transfer by that person. Section 15(1), including its proviso and explanation, provides a distinct route for permitted notified transfers and successive transfers in the specified classes, but the company's transfer was not within a notified class. Section 108(j) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 distinguishes a lessee's sublease from a subsequent transfer by a sublessee. The court approved N. M. Nayak v. Chhotalal Hariram, which held that section 15(2) validates transfers by tenants, not further derivative transfers; Anand Nivas (P.) Ltd. v. Anandji was relied on for the meaning of “tenant” as the contractual tenant.

predicates.appeal_concerns_tenant_protection_after_: The proceeding is an appeal concerning an occupant's claim to tenant protection after dispossession in execution of a decree against the tenant.
predicates.occupant_claims_retroactive_subtenancy_p: The occupant claims protection based on a measure that validates certain pre-existing sublettings or transfers.
predicates.occupant_is_later_transferee_from_subten: The occupant received the premises through a later transfer from a person who had originally taken a sublease from the tenant.
predicates.original_subtenant_not_in_possession_at_: The original subtenant was not in possession of the premises when the validating measure took effect.

issues.definition: When an occupant in an execution-dispossession tenant-protection appeal claims retroactive subtenancy protection as a later transferee from a subtenant, and the original subtenant was not in possession when the validating measure took effect, the later transferee is not protected by that validation.

issues.legal_issue: An alternative claim under the rules for permitted notified transfers cannot be entertained when it has no foundation in the pleadings or supporting material.
material_facts: The company faintly argued that it was protected under the rules concerning notified transfers.
The company had not laid a foundation for that claim in the High Court, and the record contained no material supporting it.
issues.conclusion: The court did not entertain the alternative claim under the rules concerning notified transfers.
issues.legal_principle: A contention unsupported by the case presented below and by material in the record cannot be entertained. The court identified no earlier case for this point.

predicates.appeal_includes_alternative_transfer_pro: A party raises an alternative claim to protection based on a permitted-transfer category in an appeal.
predicates.claim_lacks_foundation_in_prior_proceedi: The party did not establish the basis for that alternative claim in the proceedings below.
predicates.record_lacks_supporting_material: The record contains no material supporting the alternative claim.

issues.definition: When an appeal includes an alternative transfer-protection claim that was not founded in the proceedings below and is unsupported by the record, the claim is not entertained.
